Dear lavaan team,

I am trying to fit a model that has a latent variable 'afect' that depends on several observed variables. The challenge is that the data doesn't come from a random sample but instead each individual has weight associated.

I am getting the following error message:

Error t(diff) %*% WLS.V non-conformable arguments lavaan

when trying to fit the following model:
fitSEM31=lavaan(modelSEM31,data=new,model.type="sem",estimator="DWLS",WLS.V=diag(fact.exp$exp08),missing="listwise")

modelSEM31="afect =~ NA*P1_orden+P3_orden+P11.1_orden+P11.2_orden+P11.3_orden+edad+SEXO1+EDUC1+EDUC2+EDUC3+ESTUDIA1+CONYUGAL1+CONYUGAL2+CONYUGAL3+NSE1+NSE2+NS\
E3+NSE4+VIVIENDA1+VIVIENDA2+VIVIENDA3+VIVIENDA4";


Any idea of what is going wrong?
--
Susana

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error
parts:
First, I notice that you are freeing the first factor loading by placing NA in front of it.  This is not necessary, but what is necessary is that you identify the model by fixing the factor variance to 1.  You can just use the lavaan argument "std.lv = TRUE" to standardize your latent variable(s), which automatically allows the first factor loadings to be freely estimated.

Regarding your use of the WLS.V argument, it doesn't sound like you want to use that.  The WLS.V argument allows you to weight the matrix of parameters being estimated, not the raw data matrix (i.e., "each individual has weight associated" doesn't sound like you are trying to weight the parameter matrix).  See the ?lavaan help page for details:
  • WLS.V  --  A user provided weight matrix to be used by estimator "WLS"; if the estimator is "DWLS", only the diagonal of this matrix will be used. For a multiple group analysis, a list with a weight matrix for each group. The elements of the weight matrix should be in the following order (if all data is continuous): first the means (if a meanstructure is involved), then the lower triangular elements of the covariance matrix including the diagonal, ordered column by column. In the categorical case: first the thresholds (including the means for continuous variables), then the slopes (if any), the variances of continuous variables (if any), and finally the lower triangular elements of the correlation/covariance matrix excluding the diagonal, ordered column by column.
I haven't used the "lavaan.survey" package before, but I understand that it is designed to allow researchers to incorporate sampling weights into their lavaan analyses, so you might want to look into that.

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lavaan.survey/index.html

Terry

If the data were continuous, I think you could use the lavaan.survey
package for this. But if the data is ordinal (and your use of DWLS seems
to suggest they are), lavaan (or lavaan.survey) can not handle this
situation yet.

Yves.
